attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-04T21:42:57.170000+00:00

evidence.finding: `yum install` failed with `Error: Package: MariaDB-server-10.11.19-1.el7_9.x86_64 (mariadb) Requires: pv` — pv was not resolvable from the repos enabled at that point.

After pv became resolvable, the install failed later at GPG key import: `Retrieving key from https://archive.mariadb.org/mariadb-10.11/yum/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB` then `GPG key retrieval failed: [Errno 14] HTTPS Error 404 - Not Found`.

A third attempt shows `Complete!` on node1 (install succeeded, including pv, rsync, socat, stunnel, replacement of mariadb-libs). No node2/node3 result for this final attempt appears in the redacted record selection.

Lease expired at 2026-09-04T21:42:57Z, ~26 seconds after the node1 install completion timestamp (21:42:31). No later records (Galera config, cluster bootstrap, mysql actions, service stop/start) appear anywhere in the selected records.
113 total command records, 56 completed, 57 requested (many still in-flight/unresolved), consistent with the run being cut off mid-install rather than completing normally.

likely_causes.cause: The RHEL7 image's default enabled repos did not include EPEL (source of pv) until the executor fixed repo config between install attempt 3 and 4 — the first failure is a missing-dependency issue from incomplete repo setup, not real package unavailability.

The MariaDB 10.11 official YUM repo's GPG key URL (archive.mariadb.org/mariadb-10.11/yum/RPM-GPG-KEY-MariaDB) returned HTTP 404 at run time — either a transient MariaDB CDN/mirror issue or a stale/incorrect key path for this 10.11.19 build.

The executor used a serial, poll-with-sleep pattern (60-90s sleeps, repeated per node, repeated across 3 failed attempts) for package installation, burning nearly the whole lease on OS-level setup before any Galera-specific work could begin, leaving no time margin for the actual task.

next_attempt_guidance: Before running the real yum install, pre-validate repo setup on one node only: confirm EPEL is enabled (yum repolist shows epel) and pv resolves (yum list pv), and confirm the MariaDB repo GPG key URL is reachable (curl -I) before fanning the install out to all 3 nodes.

If the MariaDB.org GPG key URL 404s again, don't retry blindly — verify the current documented key URL/path for the 10.11 series, import from a locally cached copy, or use gpgcheck=0 only as a last-resort with awareness of the tradeoff.
Run OS package installation on all 3 nodes in parallel/background (launch then poll with short tail checks) rather than sequential 60-90s blocking sleeps repeated per node per attempt.

Budget time explicitly: if yum/repo issues aren't resolved within roughly the first 10% of the available lease window, stop repeating near-identical install attempts and switch strategy (different mirror, offline RPMs, different base image).

The actual task — Galera cluster bootstrap, safe full-cluster shutdown, wsrep-new-cluster recovery bootstrap from the node with highest seqno in grastate.dat, rejoin of the other two nodes, and write-durability verification — was never attempted in this run; treat this postmortem as covering only the environment-setup phase.
diagnosis.summary: Attempt 1 never reached Galera cluster configuration, data seeding, or the actual cold-restart maintenance procedure. The entire observed command window (21:34–21:42 UTC) was consumed retrying `yum install` for MariaDB-server on RHEL7 across node1–node3, and the cluster lease expired (21:42:57) roughly 26 seconds after the first node finally reported a successful install. No evidence exists that MariaDB/Galera was ever started, joined, had data written, or was shut down/restarted.
